facts.f: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
facts.e: Bones hold us up, protect organs like the brain and heart, and help us move.

facts.f: A newborn baby has more bones than an adult: about 270 to 300.
facts.e: As a child grows, some bones join together, leaving 206 in an adult.

facts.f: The thigh bone, called the femur, is the longest bone in the body.
facts.e: It runs from the hip to the knee and is also one of the strongest bones.

facts.f: The smallest bone in the body is the stapes, deep inside the ear.
facts.e: It is about the size of a grain of rice and helps carry sound.

facts.f: At rest, an adult's heart usually beats about 60 to 100 times a minute.
facts.e: It beats faster when you run or play, to send more blood to your muscles.

facts.f: Skin is the largest organ of the body.
facts.e: It keeps germs out, holds water in and helps control body temperature.

facts.f: The brain controls the whole body.
facts.e: It sends and receives messages through nerves, faster than you can blink.

facts.f: The left side of the brain controls the right side of the body, and the right side controls the left.
facts.e: The nerves cross over on their way between the brain and the body.

facts.f: Blood is red because of haemoglobin.
facts.e: Haemoglobin is an iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

facts.f: Red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells fight germs, and platelets help blood clot.
facts.e: Each kind of blood cell has its own important job.

facts.f: We breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.
facts.e: Our lungs pass oxygen into the blood and remove carbon dioxide from it.

facts.f: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.
facts.e: Enamel covers the outside of each tooth. It cannot grow back, so brushing protects it.

facts.f: Children have 20 milk teeth. A full set of adult permanent teeth has 32.
facts.e: Milk teeth fall out to make room for bigger, permanent teeth.

facts.f: Every person has unique fingerprints, even identical twins.
facts.e: That is why fingerprints are used to identify people.

facts.f: The small intestine is much longer than the large intestine.
facts.e: It is called 'small' because it is narrower, not shorter.

facts.f: Digestion begins in the mouth.
facts.e: Chewing breaks food into small pieces, and saliva starts breaking down starch.

facts.f: The liver is the largest internal organ and the largest gland in the body.
facts.e: It does hundreds of jobs, like storing energy and cleaning the blood.

facts.f: The kidneys clean the blood and make urine.
facts.e: Most people have two bean-shaped kidneys near the back.

facts.f: The pupil of your eye shrinks in bright light and grows in dim light.
facts.e: This controls how much light enters the eye.

facts.f: We have five main senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
facts.e: Eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin are the sense organs.

facts.f: Hair and nails are made of a protein called keratin.
facts.e: Keratin is also found in animal horns, hooves and feathers.

facts.f: The human body has more than 600 muscles.
facts.e: Muscles help us move, breathe, and even keep our heart beating.

facts.f: Muscles can only pull, not push.
facts.e: That is why they work in pairs. One pulls to bend your arm, another pulls to straighten it.

facts.f: The human heart has four chambers.
facts.e: Two upper chambers called atria and two lower chambers called ventricles.

facts.f: Covering a sneeze or cough with your elbow helps stop germs spreading.
facts.e: Sneezes and coughs spray tiny droplets that can carry germs.

facts.f: Washing hands with soap for at least 20 seconds removes germs.
facts.e: Soap breaks up the oily layer that helps germs stick to skin.

facts.f: Vaccines train the body's immune system to recognise germs.
facts.e: Then, if the real germ attacks, the body is ready to fight it quickly.

facts.f: Normal human body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.
facts.e: A temperature well above this is called a fever.

facts.f: Sleep helps the brain store what you learned during the day.
facts.e: A good night's sleep helps memory, mood and growth.

facts.f: About 60% of an adult's body is water.
facts.e: We lose water when we breathe, sweat and go to the toilet, so we need to drink every day.

facts.f: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back to it.
facts.e: Tiny vessels called capillaries connect them.

facts.f: Edward Jenner made the first vaccine, against smallpox, in 1796.
facts.e: The word 'vaccine' comes from the Latin word for cow, because he used cowpox.

facts.f: Smallpox was declared wiped out from the whole world in 1980.
facts.e: It is the first human disease to be eradicated, thanks to vaccination.

facts.f: DNA carries the instructions for building and running the body.
facts.e: It is found in almost every cell and is passed from parents to children.

facts.f: Humans usually have 23 pairs of chromosomes: 46 in all.
facts.e: Chromosomes are packages of DNA. One of each pair comes from each parent.

facts.f: The tongue can sense five basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami.
facts.e: Umami is a savoury taste, found in foods like tomatoes and mushrooms.

facts.f: The inner ear helps you keep your balance.
facts.e: Fluid in tiny tubes in the ear tells the brain which way your head is moving.

facts.f: The coloured part of the eye is called the iris.
facts.e: The iris controls the size of the pupil, the black hole in the middle.

facts.f: Our skin makes vitamin D when sunlight falls on it.
facts.e: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium to build strong bones.

facts.f: Calcium helps make bones and teeth strong.
facts.e: Milk, curd, ragi and green leafy vegetables are good sources of calcium.

facts.f: Goosebumps happen when tiny muscles at the base of each hair tighten.
facts.e: This makes the hairs stand up, often when we are cold or excited.

facts.f: A dome-shaped muscle called the diaphragm helps you breathe.
facts.e: When it moves down, air rushes into the lungs.

facts.f: Insulin, made by the pancreas, controls the level of sugar in the blood.
facts.e: People with diabetes have trouble making or using insulin.

facts.f: The heart beats about 1 lakh (100,000) times every day.
facts.e: At about 70 beats a minute, that is 70 x 60 x 24, or roughly 100,800 beats.

quiz.q: How many bones does an adult human have?
quiz.x: Adults have 206 bones. Babies are born with more, which join as they grow.

quiz.q: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
quiz.x: The femur runs from the hip to the knee.

quiz.q: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
quiz.x: Skin covers the whole body, making it the largest organ.

quiz.q: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
quiz.x: Enamel, the outer layer of teeth, is harder than bone.

quiz.q: How many milk teeth does a child have?
quiz.x: Children have 20 milk teeth; a full set of adult teeth has 32.

quiz.q: Which blood cells fight germs?
quiz.x: White blood cells are the body's defenders.

quiz.q: What gives blood its red colour?
quiz.x: Haemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that carries oxygen.

quiz.q: Which organs clean the blood and make urine?
quiz.x: Our two kidneys filter waste from the blood.

quiz.q: Where is the smallest bone in the body?
quiz.x: The stapes, in the middle ear, is the smallest bone.

quiz.q: Which gas does our body need from the air?
quiz.x: Our cells need oxygen to release energy from food.

quiz.q: What is normal human body temperature?
quiz.x: About 37 °C is normal; well above that is a fever.

quiz.q: Which vitamin does our skin make in sunlight?
quiz.x: Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D, which builds strong bones.

quiz.q: What are hair and nails made of?
quiz.x: Keratin is a tough protein, also found in horns and feathers.

quiz.q: Arteries carry blood in which direction?
quiz.x: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins bring it back.

quiz.q: Who made the first vaccine?
quiz.x: Jenner made a smallpox vaccine in 1796. Pasteur later made vaccines for rabies and other diseases.

quiz.q: How many pairs of chromosomes do humans usually have?
quiz.x: 23 pairs make 46 chromosomes in all.

quiz.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
quiz.x: Two atria on top and two ventricles below.

quiz.q: Which organ makes insulin?
quiz.x: The pancreas makes insulin, which controls blood sugar.

quiz.q: How many main senses do we have?
quiz.x: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

quiz.q: Which is the largest internal organ?
quiz.x: The liver is the largest organ inside the body.

quiz.q: The left side of the brain controls which side of the body?
quiz.x: Nerves cross over, so each side of the brain controls the opposite side of the body.
